Rejection sampler: X = floor(pow(U, -1.0/am1)) is rejected if X > RAND_INT_MAX or X < 1; 1/(a-1) is large when a is near 1, so most time is spent rejecting too-large values
Fix in random_zipf adds Umin variable to compute the U range that avoids too-large X (work backwards from RAND_INT_MAX), eliminating those values
Regression test test_zipf_a_near_1 uses n=100000 samples with a=1.0000000000001 and checks more than half of samples are below 2**62
Issue comment: a positive probability of drawing 0.0 means the rejection sampler always exits, though it may take up to about 1 in 2**53 draws
Legacy zipf implementation restored in legacy-distributions.c with am1=a-1, b=2^am1, and acceptance test V*X*(T-1)/(b-1) <= T/b
reproduction_risks: Sampling with a extremely close to 1 may take an extraordinarily long time, so a reproduction may appear to hang even when behaviour is correct
